newsitem.title: USA: Spain's Telefonica to join Concert-sources.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Telefonica to join Concert-sources.

text.p: Telefonica de Espana on Friday is to announce it will join the Concert alliance of merger partners British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp, sources close to the deal said.

They said that BT will take a minority stake in Telefonica and added the Spanish company is expected eventually to leave its Unisource alliance with AT&T Corp and three other European telecom companies.
"The announcement will be made on Friday from Madrid," one of the sources said, declining to be identified.
Neither BT nor MCI would comment. It was not immediately possible to contact Telefonica.

The sources said it is not certain whether or not Telefonica will separately take a stake in Concert, which was the name chosen by BT and MCI for their new company when they announced their $20 billion merger in November.

The news was widely expected. The alliance earlier this week signed up Portugal Telecom to join Concert and the Portuguese company let slip in its own announcement a reference to Telefonica joining up with MCI.
For Telefonica it means joining the big league of telecommunications groups and the BT stake means it will be more tightly bound to its partners than with Unisource.
It will get access to the 40 million Spanish speakers in the U.S. and in return offers a ticket into Latin America where its Telefonica Internacional unit had sales last year of $2.4 billion.
"It is another positive for BT, MCI and Concert," said Barry Sine, an analyst at SBC Warburg.

MCI and BT will be able to leave the Spanish market to its new partner and cut down the number of markets it is pushing into simultaneously with the 1998 liberalisation of European telecommunications.
"France and Germany are obviously more of a priority," said Sine.

For AT&T, struggling in a highly competitive market at home, this undermines its efforts to build a powerful international alliance to bring in business from multinational firms and to enter new markets in Europe and Latin America.
"For AT&T it is less of a factor. Yes it is a loss, but AT&T must keep its priority as fixing its problems in the U.S.," Sine said.
Telefonica, Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV, Sweden's Telia and Swiss Telecom each own a 25 percent stake in Unisource, which is affiliated to AT&T.
Concert is also competing with Global One, an alliance of Deutsche Telekom AG, France Telecom and the third largest U.S. long distance telephone carrier, Sprint Corp .
